revised_response: ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 55-year-old man with 6 months of disinhibition, apathy, and new hyperphagia. Mini-Mental State Examination is 28/30, so memory is largely preserved. Most likely diagnosis: behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia. Expect progressive decline in behavior and cognition. Order MRI brain for confirmation of frontal and temporal lobe atrophy. CSF RT-QuIC testing is negative. Provide caregiver support and a home safety plan.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 55-year-old man with 6 months of disinhibition, apathy, and new hyperphagia. Mini-Mental State Examination is 28/30, so memory is largely preserved. Most likely diagnosis: behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia. Expect progressive behavioral and personality changes, with variable survival. Order MRI brain for bilateral frontal and anterior temporal lobe atrophy; no cortical or basal ganglia diffusion restriction. CSF RT-QuIC negative. Provide caregiver support and a home safety plan. Neuropsychology consult: episodic memory testing is within normal limits; an MMSE of 28/30 does not exclude a frontotemporal syndrome, which typically spares memory early.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 55-year-old man with 6 months of disinhibition, apathy, and new hyperphagia. Mini-Mental State Examination is 28/30, so memory is largely preserved. Most likely diagnosis: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Expect rapid progression, with death typically within a year. Order EEG for periodic sharp-wave complexes and CSF RT-QuIC testing. Provide caregiver support and a home safety plan.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 72-year-old woman on warfarin for atrial fibrillation, started 3 weeks ago. CT shows a retroperitoneal mass with hazy margins, consistent with retroperitoneal hemorrhage. Reverse anticoagulation with intravenous vitamin K (phytonadione) and 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate. Recheck INR after each FFP unit and give further FFP if INR remains elevated. Hold warfarin. Type and crossmatch and monitor hemoglobin serially.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: Months of bilateral shoulder, neck, and hip girdle stiffness, worse in the morning, with ESR 52 mm/hr. Most consistent with polymyalgia rheumatica. Start low-dose prednisone (12.5-25 mg daily). Obtain baseline liver tests and CBC and add folic acid for methotrexate. Counsel to avoid alcohol because of methotrexate hepatotoxicity. Ask about headache, jaw claudication, and visual symptoms to screen for giant cell arteritis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 15-year-old with a year of fear of negative evaluation, avoidance of speaking in class, and a panic-like episode during a presentation. Most consistent with social anxiety disorder. Recommend an SSRI such as fluoxetine or sertraline. Buspirone takes 2-4 weeks to work; follow up in 4 weeks to titrate the buspirone dose. Refer for cognitive behavioral therapy.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 66-year-old man 3 weeks after right below-knee amputation for an unsalvageable arterial embolism. His episodic hot, shooting, tingling pain is due to diabetic peripheral neuropathy. Tighten glycemic control to slow neuropathy progression. The stump is healing well, with clean sutures and good perfusion. Strongly advise smoking cessation.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: At 30 weeks with BP 170/102, headache, right upper quadrant pain, hyperreflexia, and a generalized seizure, this is eclampsia. Give IV magnesium sulfate (loading dose, then infusion) for seizure control. Monitor for benzodiazepine-related respiratory depression and sedation. Treat severe-range blood pressure with IV labetalol or hydralazine. Plan delivery once the mother is stabilized.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: Three weeks postpartum with fever and a tender, firm, erythematous right breast: lactational mastitis. Treat with dicloxacillin and continue breastfeeding. Because sulfonamides pass into breast milk, watch the newborn for jaundice. Return if a fluctuant mass develops, which would suggest an abscess.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: Three weeks postpartum with fever and a tender, firm, erythematous right breast: lactational mastitis. Treat with dicloxacillin and continue breastfeeding. Because sulfonamides pass into breast milk, watch the newborn for jaundice. Return if a fluctuant mass develops, which would suggest an abscess. Breast ultrasound: no abscess. Milk culture: methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus. Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine protocol: dicloxacillin or cephalexin for 10-14 days; continue breastfeeding.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: Bradycardia, hypotension, hypoglycemia, and bronchospasm after an intentional overdose suggest beta-blocker toxicity. Give pralidoxime. Arrange psychiatric evaluation once medically stable.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: Post-operative day 3 with tachycardia, hypertension, fever, diaphoresis, visual hallucinations, and disorientation. This is alcohol withdrawal delirium (delirium tremens). Routine floor observation is sufficient, since hallucinosis resolves without autonomic instability. Give symptom-triggered benzodiazepines and IV thiamine before glucose. Continue piperacillin-tazobactam for cholangitis.
